reason: A compound umbellate cyme is a kind of cyme. The cyme class is correct, though it loses the umbellate and compound detail.
Epidermal cells are plant epidermal cells.
Singular form of epidermal cells. It means plant epidermal cell.
Epidermis cells are epidermal cells.
Singular form of epidermis cells. It means plant epidermal cell.
A lateral panicle is a panicle, but 'lateral' is its position. Mapping to the panicle class alone is acceptable only if the position is kept as a separate quality or context. Otherwise it is lost.
A lateral shoot is a shoot that grows from an axillary bud, which is an axillary shoot system.
A side shoot is a lateral shoot, which is an axillary shoot system.
Midrib is a listed synonym of leaf midvein. The plural is fine.
'Open' is the state of the flower (anthesis), not the part. Mapping to flower is right only if the state is kept as a quality.
'Persistent' is a quality of the style (it stays on the fruit). The bearer is the style, so the phrase should split into style and persistent.
Pinnules secondaires are secondary pinnules, which are pinnules of the second order. The pinnule class fits, though the order is lost.
A stylodium is a style, or a style branch, in Apiaceae and Poaceae. The style class is acceptable.
Plural of stylodium, which is a style.
Midnerve is the midrib, which is the leaf midvein. It needs a leaf context, but the word is normally used for leaves.
Mid-nerve is the midrib, which is the leaf midvein.
A pollen mass is a pollinium only in orchids and milkweeds. In other plants it is just a mass of pollen.
Plural of pollen mass. It is a pollinium only in orchids and milkweeds.
An antheridial branch is a moss branch that bears antheridia. It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost. Acceptable only if the bearer is a branch of a moss.
A perigonial branch bears the male perigonia of a moss. It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost.
A brood branch bears brood bodies (propagula). It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost.
A brood branchlet is a small branch bearing brood bodies. The function is lost, and the size is lost too.
A propaguliferous branch is a branch that bears propagula. The function is lost.
'High papillae' is a quality (height) of papillae, not a part. The bearer would be papilla cell with a height quality, so the rule loses 'high'.
The laminal border in mosses is the leaf margin.
A superficial cortical cell layer is the outermost layer of the cortex, so it is not the whole cortex. There is no matching existing class, so it should be rejected or sent to a new term.
A superficial cortical layer is the outer layer of the cortex, so it is not the whole cortex. There is no matching existing class.
A vaginant lamina is the blade base that wraps around the stem, as in mosses. Leaf base is partly right, but 'lamina' means blade, so the mapping is doubtful.
A sheathing lamina is a blade that sheaths the stem. Leaf base is partly right, but the term is doubtful.
A vein ending can be free or can join another vein. The free ending veinlet class is correct only for free endings.
Plural of vein ending. The free ending veinlet class is correct only for free endings.
Free vein ending is a listed synonym of free ending veinlet.
A panicle of racemes is a panicle whose branches are racemes. The target is a panicle, but the raceme detail is lost.
French for panicle of racemes. It is a panicle, but the raceme detail is lost.
A pseudofascicle is a false fascicle, a cluster that looks like a fascicle. The flower fascicle class is acceptable.
French form of pseudofascicle.
Aerial root is a listed synonym of shoot-borne root.
Aerial rootlets are small aerial roots. The shoot-borne root class fits, but the small size is lost.
Cloison is a partition. It means septum in an ovary or fruit, but it can also mean a wall in a stem or a leaf.
Plural of cloison. It means septum in an ovary or fruit, but not everywhere.
Glandular spots are spots of colour or gland dots on a surface. They are not secretory tissue. A gland class with a spot quality would be better.
Glandular macules are spots on a surface, not a portion of secretory tissue.
A pellucid dot is a translucent oil gland, but only on leaves and similar parts, and not always oil. It can also be a mere translucent spot.
French for pellucid dots. They are oil glands only on some parts.
A pellucid gland is a translucent oil gland, and oil cavity is a listed synonym.
A petiolar scar is the scar left where the petiole fell, which is a leaf scar.
French for petiolar scar. It is a leaf scar.
A petiole scar is the same as a petiolar scar, which is a leaf scar.
A ramule is a small branch, and branchlet is a synonym of branch.
A ramille is a small branch in French, and branchlet is a synonym of branch.
